A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the levels of antibiotics in sewage in Hong Kong and in Shenzhen are generally low, but there are some regional variations in the concentrations and the antibiotic profiles of sewage.

the removal of antibiotics in STPs in Hong Kongs is generally good, and the concentrations of antibiotics in the effluents from Hong Kongs STPs would not cause adverse effects on the receiving environment.

concentrations of antibiotics in sewage effluents from Hong Kong and Shenzhens STPs are generally lower than the predicted environmental concentration (PECs), and therefore, the risk of antibiotics causing adverse effects on the environment is considered to be low.
The main takeaway from our work is that
STPs can effectively remove antibiotics from wastewater, but the extent of the removal depends on the chemical properties of the antibiotic and the treatment processes used.

the concentrations of most antibiotics measured in influent samples were lower than the corresponding predicted no effect concentrations, suggesting that the concentrations of antibiotics measured at these STPs are not likely to cause adverse effects to the wastewater treatment processes.
